translations.answer: The mutex was fixed to list the storage controllers, preventing changes during non-real-time callback reads; loading itself is not part of the real-time path. Therefore, the comment 'lock controllers' cannot directly infer that the update is locked. However, the original thread lacks a delay benchmark, and the target version still applies path auditing and cycle measurement. The credibility is limited as there is no formal cross-verification or independent replication available.
translations.applicability: Applies to ros2_control PR #820 post-merge, and controller_manager/diagnostic_updater lock semantics at the time; other versions require re-tracing the call path.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-verification or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: The project member cited the controller_manager loading path, indicating that the lock prevents loading of new controllers.
translations.details.attempts.1: The author replied after seeing the call path explanation, stating the issue was clear.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: All read/write points on controllers_lock_ were checked to confirm it protects the list of controllers, not individual controller objects or the update() execution.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Distinguished between non-real-time 'load controller' operations and real-time controller update paths.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: No need to delete diagnostic functions due to the code; the issue should be resolved by verifying the lock contention based on the protected object and call path.
translations.details.environments.0: Original post corresponds to ros2_control PR #820 and the controller_manager master branch at the time; ROS 2 distribution not specified.
translations.details.limits.0: The thread only explains lock semantics and call path, but does not provide delay measurement or worst-case blocking time under diagnostic callbacks.
translations.details.limits.1: The conclusion corresponds to the 2022 implementation; subsequent versions must re-examine the lock usage location.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The original author accepted the explanation; the issue was closed as completed, and the project member later clarified that the lock is on the controller list, not the controller itself.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Will the diagnostic_updater lock the controller execution and affect real-time performance when holding controllers_lock_?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Call path analysis can only exclude misinterpretation in true machine hard real-time WBC; control cycle jitter must still be measured under worst-case diagnostic loads.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The comment 'lock controllers' is too simplistic, potentially misinterpreting 'locking the list' as 'locking the execution'.
translations.details.symptoms.0: The code comment says 'lock controllers', and controllers_lock_ has a std::lock_guard<std::recursive_mutex> created, suggesting a diagnostic callback lock on controllers.
